problem:
$$
⟨\,(1-\operatorname{cos}⁡y)\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\text{_______}\,,\,(1-\operatorname{cos}⁡y)\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ⟩
$$

 

The fundamental vector product of the surface of revolution generated by rotating the curve $x=1-\operatorname{cos}⁡y$ by $2\pi $ radians about the $y$-axis for $y\in [0,\pi ]$ is given above. What is the $2$nd component of the product?
worked_solution:
Notice that $x=1-\operatorname{cos}⁡y\ge 0$ for all $y\in [0,\pi ].$ The parametrization of our surface of revolution is

$$
\begin{aligned}r=⟨f(y)\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,y,\,f(y)\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ⟩,\,(y,\theta )\in D\end{aligned}
$$

where $f(y)=1-\operatorname{cos}⁡y,$ and 

$$
D={(y,\theta )\,:\,0\le y\le \pi ,\,0\le \theta <2\pi }.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{y}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂y},\,\frac{∂y}{∂y},\,\frac{∂z}{∂y}⟩=⟨{f}^{′}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,1,\,{f}^{′}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ⟩ \\ {r}_{\theta }^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂\theta },\,\frac{∂y}{∂\theta },\,\frac{∂z}{∂\theta }⟩=⟨-f\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,0,\,f\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{y}^{′}\times {r}_{\theta }^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ {f}^{′}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & 1 & {f}^{′}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\ -f\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & 0 & f\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}1 & {f}^{′}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\ 0 & f\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & {f}^{′}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\ -f\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & f\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & 1 \\ -f\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & 0\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨f\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,-{f}^{′}f{cos}^{2}⁡\theta -{f}^{′}f{sin}^{2}⁡\theta ,\,f\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ⟩ \\  & =⟨f\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,-{f}^{′}f,\,f\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Since $f=1-\operatorname{cos}⁡y,$ we obtain ${f}^{′}=\operatorname{sin}⁡y.$ So, finally, we conclude that the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{y}^{′}\times {r}_{\theta }^{′}=⟨(1-\operatorname{cos}⁡y)\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡y(1-\operatorname{cos}⁡y),\,(1-\operatorname{cos}⁡y)\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
